primary_source.headline: Durga Puja pandal stampede gives Mamata's TMC a ‘bhaipo’ in BJP to target
primary_source.content: Kolkata: The stampede at a Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata has triggered a war of words in West Bengal politics, as the alleged association of two ruling Bharatiya Janata Party leaders and Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari’s nephew with the organisers provided fresh ammunition to the Mamata Banerjee faction of the Trinamool Congress to attack the government.Suvendu, himself, on October 12, inaugurated the Chorebagan Sarbojanin Durgotsab Samity’s pandal, where a stampede left 19 people dead and more than 20 injured on Sunday. The narrow entry and exit alleyways, limited space and inadequate crowd-control measures, deliberately dim lighting to match the pandal's theme, a sudden influx of visitors seeking shelter from the evening rain, and alleged lapses in police arrangements are blamed for the disaster.With Suvendu’s nephew, Debdeep Adhikari, being the chief patron of the organising committee, the Mamata All India Trinamool Congress, the TMC faction led by Mamata Banerjee, finally found a ‘bhaipo’ in the ruling BJP to train the guns on.&nbsp;“Guess who is closely associated with the Chorebagan Puja Pandal? CM Suvendu Adhikari’s BHAIPO,” the MAITC posted on X soon after the disaster. “When are you going to put your criminal nephew behind bars, Suvendu Babu?” posted Abhishek Banerjee, who has been at the receiving end of the ‘bhaipo (nephew)’ taunt ever since his ‘pisi (aunt)’, Mamata Banerjee, inducted him into the party she founded.The tragedy raised questions about whether the organisers had made adequate safety arrangements for the large crowds expected at the pandal. Its narrow entry and exit passageways, sloping route through the structure, and deliberately dim lighting intended to complement its theme may have heightened the risk of overcrowding and slowed visitor movement. The sudden influx of people seeking shelter from the evening rain further compounded the danger, while questions were raised about the police's preparedness to regulate the crowds and respond to the emergency.Not only Debdeep, but two other BJP leaders were also associated with this year’s Durga Puja of the Chorebagan Sarbojanin Durgotsav Samity, legislator Vijay Ojha as chairman and the saffron party’s North Kolkata district unit president, Tamoghna Ghosh, as chief adviser.The six people arrested by police after the incident include the secretary Raj Kumar Sewda and the vice president of the organising committee Santanu Dubey, but none are linked to the BJP.“The CM himself inaugurated Chorebagan Puja Pandal. Did he not look into security arrangements when he visited the pandal? Won’t he be held accountable for every single life lost?” the Mamata faction of the TMC asked, questioning whether the police would take any action against Debdeep, Vijay and Tamoghna.Soon after the stampede on Saturday, Suvendu and Health Minister Sharadwat Mukherjee rushed to Kolkata Medical College and Hospital, where the injured and deceased were initially taken. The chief minister visited the stampede site in the pre-dawn hours of Sunday.“Attempts are being made by some people to reap political dividends from such a tragedy. They will not succeed. The families of the deceased and injured told me that they had full faith in the state government and me,” Suvendu said on Sunday. He added that a probe was underway and the government would not spare anyone found responsible for the disaster. “No one should indulge in politics over death,” he said.&nbsp;Kolkata stampede | 'CM himself inaugurated Chorebagan puja pandal, will he be held accountable?': Mamata AITC attacks Suvendu govtHe sought to turn the tables on his predecessor, Mamata Banerjee, and the TMC government she had headed.&nbsp;The chief minister cited several tragedies during the TMC’s tenure, including the collapse of an under-construction flyover in north Kolkata in 2016, which killed seven people, and the collapse of Majherhat Bridge in 2018, which killed three. He also referred to the Panihati festival incident in July 2022, in which three people died; the electrocution deaths of nine people during waterlogging in Kolkata after heavy rain ahead of Durga Puja in 2025; and flash floods in North Bengal that year, which killed around 100 people.“What was the then chief minister doing?” Suvendu questioned, hitting back at Mamata.&nbsp;“This is not the time to indulge in a political blame game,” Samik Bhattacharya, the state BJP chief, said, responding to the Opposition's criticism. &nbsp;&nbsp;The Opposition, however, is not ready to relent. “Where were the police when the incident took place? There was no response even after calls were made to the police control room,” Subhankar Sarkar, president of the West Bengal Pradesh Congress Committee, said.What further sharpened criticism of the city police and the state government is that, over the past few days, cops in several places were seen evicting or trying to evict bookstalls set up by the Communist Party of India (Marxist) near the Durga Puja pandals. Mohammed Salim, the state secretary of the CPI(M), questioned the priorities of the police, stating that the residents living near the pandal of the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja Samity complained about a lack of police to manage the crowd as well as the unavailability of an adequate number of ambulances to take the injured to hospital after the disaster.&nbsp;As in several other Durga Puja organising clubs across West Bengal, the leadership of the Chorebagan Sarbojanin Durgotsab Samity changed after the TMC’s defeat in the Assembly elections earlier this year and the BJP’s rise to power. Jayanta Bandopadhyay, who was known to be associated with the TMC, was removed from the puja committee’s leadership, although he had managed the festival for several years. Jayanta had also performed the Khunti Puja, the ceremony marking the start of pandal construction, before he and others were sidelined and a new committee comprising people linked to the ruling BJP was formed. The new committee subsequently performed a second Khunti Puja in the presence of several BJP leaders.

stories.primary_headline: Tamil Nadu: ‘Thenisai Thendral’ Deva laid to rest amid tears, tributes

primary_source.headline: Tamil Nadu: ‘Thenisai Thendral’ Deva laid to rest amid tears, tributes
primary_source.content: Ranipet (Tamil Nadu): Veteran Tamil music composer and singer Deva, popularly known as 'Thenisai Thendral', was laid to rest with full state honours at his family farmland in Sakkaramallur near Arcot, Ranipet district, on Sunday.He was 75.Deva died of a heart attack in Chennai on the morning of October 17.His mortal remains were taken from his Chennai residence to the farmland, where the final rites were performed.Thousands of people gathered at the site to pay their last respects to the celebrated music director.Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay had visited Deva's residence in Chennai to pay his respects and announced that the funeral would be held with state honours in recognition of the composer's contribution to the music industry.Revenue and police officials oversaw arrangements for the ceremony at Sakkaramallur.‘Thenisai Thendral’ Deva (1950-2026): The maestro who took gaana to the masses Relatives and villagers recalled Deva's enduring connection to his roots, saying he regularly visited his native village during festivals such as Pongal and contributed to local initiatives, including funding the construction of a Sri Ranganathar temple.Born Devanesan Chokkalingam, Deva had a career spanning nearly four decades and composed music for more than 400 films in Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam.Before turning to films, Deva was an employee of the Tamil Nadu government’s Public Works Department (PWD).He made his entry as a composer in 1986 with 'Mattukkara Mannaru', which did not fare well in theatres, though its songs found a loyal audience over time.'Manasukketha Maharasa' (1989), starring Ramarajan and Seetha, was the film that first drew attention to his work. His real breakthrough, however, came in 1990 with the Prashanth-starrer 'Vaigasi Poranthachu', which won him widespread acclaim.Deva rose to prominence in the late 1980s and 1990s with his high-energy, folk-rooted tunes, and is widely credited with bringing the ‘gaana’ genre into mainstream Tamil cinema.Few composers in Tamil cinema are as closely identified with one genre as Deva is with 'gaana', the urban folk music born in the working-class neighbourhoods of North Chennai.He worked with nearly every leading star of his time, among them Vijayakanth, Sarathkumar, Vijay and Ajith, and delivered some of the biggest hits of their careers.Among his chartbusters were the Rajinikanth films ‘Annamalai’, ‘Baashha’ and ‘Arunachalam’, and the Kamal Haasan outings ‘Avvai Shanmugi’, ‘Pammal K Sambandam’ and ‘Panchathanthiram’.His death drew tributes from political leaders, members of the film fraternity and fans across Tamil Nadu.

primary_source.content: Mumbai: Exactly a month after Sahil Wakode, a student of Indian Institute of Technology-Bombay died by suicide, students and activists staged a protest outside the institute’s Powai campus on Sunday, however, police dispersed the mob and detained several of them.The parents of Sahil—Ravindra Wakode and Sonali Wakode—too were part of the protests.&nbsp;On 18 September, Sahil (20), a second-year student from Energy Science and Engineering Department, was caught allegedly using a mobile phone to access ChatGPT during a mid-semester examination. However, his body was later found in his hostel room.&nbsp;The case is being investigated by the&nbsp;Crime Branch-CID, which has taken over investigations from the Powai police station.&nbsp;Sahil Wakode death: Protesting IIT Bombay students claim detention, use of excessive force by policeThe parents are demanding action and arrest of&nbsp; Prof Shireesh Kedare, the Director of&nbsp; Indian Institute of Technology-Bombay and Prof Suryanarayana Doolla, a faculty member of the premier institute’s Energy Science and Engineering Department.Meanwhile, the Congress once again backed the parents and said that it will ensure that Sahil Wakode gets justice. Sahil Wakode, a backward-class student at the IIT Mumbai institution, did not commit suicide; it was "an institutional murder."“Even though a month has passed since this incident, no action has been taken against anyone yet. In the past 13 months, 4 students in this institution have died by suicide. After Sahil's death, students in the institution are protesting, and the police are committing atrocities against them, beating them. On whose orders are the police committing atrocities in the institution's premises? All these things must stop. An inquiry must be conducted quickly, and strict action must be taken against those responsible for Sahil's murder,” said Mumbai Congress president and MP Prof Varsha Gaikwad.&nbsp;“RSS ideology has infiltrated this prestigious IIT institution, and this is not good for the education sector. Keep educational institutions away from political ideologies,” she added.&nbsp;A delegation from the All India Independent Scheduled Castes Association arrived at the IIT Bombay gates around noon, seeking to pay respects to Sahil.&nbsp;

brief_bullets: Exactly one month after the tragic suicide of twenty-year-old Sahil Wakode, a second-year energy science student at the Indian Institute of Technology-Bombay, grieving parents Ravindra and Sonali Wakode joined students and activists outside the Powai campus to demand accountability. Wakode's death followed accusations of using ChatGPT during an examination, prompting the Crime Branch-CID to take over the investigation from local police amid mounting protests and allegations of institutional negligence. Demonstrators and political figures, including Mumbai Congress president Varsha Gaikwad, have labeled the tragedy an institutional murder while demanding the immediate arrests of IIT Bombay Director Prof. Shireesh Kedare and faculty member Prof. Suryanarayana Doolla. Police ultimately dispersed the demonstration and detained several protesters, drawing sharp criticism over the use of excessive force against those seeking justice for backward-class students within elite academic institutions.
why_it_matters_bullets: This incident exposes deep-seated systemic vulnerabilities and recurring mental health crises within elite Indian higher education institutions, highlighting urgent calls for structural reform, unbiased accountability, and better safeguarding of marginalized student populations.

This stark demographic disparity underscores a critical failure in urban planning, pedestrian infrastructure, and public transit safety measures. State authorities and transport organizations face mounting pressure to reevaluate existing road safety frameworks to better protect non-motorized commuters and vehicular passengers. The figures indicate that while general enforcement might be reducing high-speed collisions, infrastructural designs continue to endanger individuals navigating roads on foot or relying on public transport.
why_it_matters_bullets: This persistent vulnerability among female pedestrians and passengers highlights a critical blind spot in regional safety initiatives, signaling that current infrastructure investments fail to protect non-drivers. Addressing this disparity is vital for urban planners and policymakers striving to create genuinely inclusive and secure public transit ecosystems.

primary_source.headline: '56-inch ka seena kahan hai': Rahul Gandhi slams Modi-Shah, CEC over 'vote chori'
primary_source.content: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Sunday accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of orchestrating alleged “vote theft” behind the scenes, claiming that Union Home Minister Amit Shah operationalised it and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar implemented it.Addressing a rally in Margao in South Goa on the concluding day of the Congress's 'Goy Rakhon Yatra', Gandhi alleged that Modi, Shah and Kumar were facing mounting pressure over the party's allegations of electoral malpractice.“There is no confusion anymore. Gyanesh Kumar implements the vote theft, Amit Shah operationalises it, and Prime Minister Narendra Modi does the entire planning from behind the scenes,” Gandhi said.The Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha warned that the three would face justice over the alleged irregularities. He also claimed that the Congress had evidence of electoral malpractice in several states, including Madhya Pradesh, Haryana, Karnataka, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, West Bengal and Assam.“PM Modi, Amit Shah and CEC Gyanesh Kumar will face justice and pay the price for what they have done,” he said.Gandhi had led protests against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise and Kumar in New Delhi. He alleged that opposition votes had been deleted, votes added in favour of the ruling party, and voters shifted between districts or brought in from other states.Claiming that more than 45 defamation cases had been filed against him, including by people associated with Modi and Shah, Gandhi said no case had been filed over his allegations of vote theft. He suggested that the government was reluctant to pursue the matter legally because it could lead to a full-fledged legal battle.Urging voters to give the Congress a full majority in the 2027 Goa Assembly elections, Gandhi called on party workers to continue engaging with people across the state.Rahul Gandhi to address Goa rally as Congress wraps up 28-day 'Goy Rakhon Yatra'“You think about Goa. In Delhi, in a short while, we will deal with Narendra Modi and Amit Shah. You don't need to worry about that. The work is underway; their expiry date is approaching,” he said.Gandhi also accused the BJP-led Union government of favouring industrialists Gautam Adani and Mukesh Ambani by awarding them infrastructure projects, land and other economic opportunities in exchange for political support and publicity.“This is their system. This is how their system works: give billionaires money, give them contracts, give them land. In return, the billionaires do their marketing,” he alleged.Turning to Goa, Gandhi accused the state government of taking land from farmers and economically weaker sections and transferring it to outsiders and associates. He alleged that the cancellation of the regional master plan had enabled the government to facilitate such transfers, putting the state's natural resources and cultural heritage at risk.“Goa is a paradise, one of the most beautiful places in the country, with a great culture,” he said, alleging that its land was being handed over to billionaires.The Congress leader further claimed that Goa had the country's highest unemployment rate, forcing young people to seek opportunities abroad. He accused the BJP government of dismantling the state's employment structure and described its functioning as a “special Goa model of corruption”, drawing a comparison with the Gujarat model associated with Modi.On education, Gandhi criticised the alleged use of force against student protesters in Delhi and accused the BJP and the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) of influencing university appointments. He said students were raising concerns over electoral malpractice, unemployment, education costs and inflation.“This country does not belong to any one organisation. This country does not belong to the RSS. This country does not belong to the BJP. This country belongs to the people of India,” he said.Gandhi added that Goa belonged to its people, not its chief minister or ministers, and called for access to education, healthcare and employment, alongside environmental protection.Taking a swipe at the Prime Minister, Gandhi questioned the absence of Modi's often-cited “56-inch seena”, saying he could not stand in front of his political opponents.He urged Congress workers to continue the party's fight against the BJP's ideology beyond the conclusion of the yatra.The 27-day 'Goy Rakhon Yatra', led by Goa Congress leaders Yuri Alemao and Girish Chodankar, began on September 22 and covered all 40 Assembly constituencies in the coastal state. The party said the campaign aimed to protect Goa's land, environment, cultural heritage and identity while strengthening its grassroots presence ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.(With PTI Inputs)

primary_source.headline: 'Couldn't prevent regime change within Shiv Sena': Maharashtra CM Fadnavis takes dig at Uddhav Thackeray
primary_source.content: Mumbai: A day after Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray backed the ‘regime change’ call, Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Sunday took a dig at him saying he could not prevent a regime change in his own party. Fadnavis was referring to the June-July 2022 rebellion in the Shiv Sena led by Eknath Shinde — who toppled Thackeray’s Maha Vikas Aghadi government with the help of BJP to become the Chief Minister. Slamming Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Thackeray on Saturday said: “Yes we are ready for a regime change…particularly If right to express ourselves through vote and right to protest is being taken away then we have to change regime.”Uddhav Thackeray backs Prashant Bhushan's regime change call, cites curbs on voting, protest rightsHowever, Fadnavis, on Sunday hit back at Thackeray, a former ally, who is now a key leader of the Congress-led INDIA opposition bloc. "Firstly, if Uddhav Thackeray could not prevent a 'regime change' within the Shiv Sena itself, I fail to understand what other 'regime change' he is referring to,” said Fadnavis, a senior BJP leader. "When his party abandoned Hindutva and discarded the ideals of the ‘Hindu Hriday Samrat' and Shiv Sena supremo Balasaheb Thackeray, it caused such an upheaval within his own ranks that those who wished to remain true to Balasaheb’s vision formed the 'real' Shiv Sena,” said Fadnavis. “My clear message is — stop challenging the Constitution of India. Decisions here will be made in Parliament, in accordance with the Constitution—not on the streets,” he said, adding: “If you want a regime change, you have to contest polls, win the hearts of the people, and secure a mandate.”

stories.primary_headline: Wikipedia often gets taken for granted – but its history is fascinating, and its future is fragile

primary_source.headline: Wikipedia often gets taken for granted – but its history is fascinating, and its future is fragile
primary_source.content: Wikipedia’s 68m articles have been consulted trillions of times. Not bad for a website that has barely changed since it was founded 20 years agoA few years ago, I was struck by the tension between how Wikipedia was used, and how it was talked about. Everyone was on it all the time, and yet its reputation had stalled at “don’t trust it”, because it was the “free encyclopedia that anyone can edit”.Clearly people were trusting it, so much so it had become part of the fabric of everyday life since it was founded by Jimmy Wales and Larry Sanger in 2001. But despite the fact it now has been consulted trillions of times by billions of people (English Wikipedia alone is 5.2bn words long), it inspires an odd lack of curiosity. Even people donating to Wikipedia might say the money was “for the factcheckers”, though there aren’t any – not paid ones, anyway. Meanwhile, the internet in the social media era had begun to feel like a much uglier place, and some digital nostalgia was setting in: here was this holdover that had somehow survived; a website that functions – and even looks – much the same as it did 20 years ago.
